blocks.content: This closing topic connects health checks directly back to the restartPolicy field covered in the Pods module, a liveness probe failure does not have its own separate restart logic, it triggers exactly the same mechanism.

As covered in the Pod Restart Policy topic, every Pod has a restartPolicy: Always, OnFailure, or Never, governing what happens whenever a container exits, or, as covered here, whenever it is killed by a failed liveness probe.

blocks.alt: The exact same three options covered back in the Pods module

blocks.content: 2. A Liveness Failure Triggers the Same Mechanism
blocks.text: 2. A Liveness Failure Triggers the Same Mechanism

blocks.content: This is genuinely important to understand precisely: when a liveness probe fails and kubelet kills the container, what happens next is governed by exactly the same restartPolicy field, there is no separate, probe-specific restart logic at all.

blocks.alt: No separate logic for probe-triggered kills, it is the exact same restartPolicy mechanism

blocks.content: 3. The Surprising Consequence of restartPolicy: Never
blocks.text: 3. The Surprising Consequence of restartPolicy: Never

blocks.content: This produces a genuinely non-obvious result worth knowing: if a Pod's restartPolicy is Never, a failed liveness probe kills the container, and it simply stays dead, no restart happens at all, a liveness probe configured on a Pod with this policy provides essentially no self-healing benefit.

blocks.alt: A genuinely surprising outcome, the container just stays dead, with no restart at all

blocks.content: 4. Why This Fits Deployments So Naturally
blocks.text: 4. Why This Fits Deployments So Naturally

blocks.content: This is exactly why liveness probes are so commonly paired with Deployments, covered in their own module, a Deployment's Pods use restartPolicy: Always, so a liveness probe failure reliably triggers a real, meaningful restart, delivering the self-healing behavior you would actually expect.

blocks.alt: The pairing that actually makes liveness probes deliver real, meaningful self-healing

blocks.content: 5. Why Jobs Use Liveness Probes Differently
blocks.text: 5. Why Jobs Use Liveness Probes Differently

blocks.content: Jobs, covered in the DaemonSet & Jobs module, typically use OnFailure or Never, and are meant to run to completion rather than indefinitely, liveness probes are used far less commonly with Jobs, since the whole "keep this running forever" framing a liveness probe assumes simply does not fit a workload meant to finish.

blocks.alt: A workload shape where the assumptions behind liveness probes largely do not apply

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A liveness probe failure does not have its own restart logic, it triggers the exact same restartPolicy mechanism covered in the Pods module.

With restartPolicy: Never, a failed liveness check simply stays dead, no restart at all, which is exactly why liveness probes pair so naturally with Deployments (Always) and far less naturally with Jobs.
